what_its_for: Brimonidine eye drops are used to lower pressure inside your eye. High eye pressure can lead to a condition called glaucoma, which can damage your vision over time. Some forms of brimonidine are also used as a cream to reduce facial redness caused by rosacea, or as eye drops to reduce redness in the eyes.
how_to_take: For eye drops: Wash your hands thoroughly before use. Tilt your head back, pull your lower eyelid down gently to create a small pocket, and place the prescribed number of drops into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye with your finger. This helps keep the medicine in your eye and reduces side effects. Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye, fingers, or any surface to keep it clean. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 to 15 minutes between each medication. For skin cream: Apply a thin layer to the affected areas of your face once daily as directed by your doctor. Avoid getting the cream in your eyes, mouth, or nose.
dosing: For glaucoma eye drops: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye or eyes, 3 times a day, spaced about 8 hours apart (for example, morning, afternoon, and evening). For rosacea cream: Apply a pea-sized amount to the affected areas of your face once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or use extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store brimonidine eye drops and cream at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle or tube tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid wearing soft contact lenses while using brimonidine eye drops, or wait at least 15 minutes after using the drops before putting your lenses in, as the preservative in the drops can be absorbed by soft lenses. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause blurred vision or drowsiness. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness. Avoid getting the eye drops or cream in your mouth or nose. For the skin cream, avoid applying to irritated, broken, or sunburned skin.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe eye pain, redness, or irritation that gets worse; sudden changes in your vision; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; very low blood pressure symptoms such as dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting; a slow or irregular heartbeat; unusual tiredness or weakness; or if your eye pressure does not seem to be controlled. If you accidentally swallow brimonidine, call Poison Control immediately at 1-800-222-1222.
when_it_works: Brimonidine eye drops begin to lower eye pressure within about 1 hour after use, with the greatest effect occurring within 2 hours. Your doctor will monitor your eye pressure with regular check-up appointments to make sure the medication is working properly. For the rosacea cream, you may notice a reduction in facial redness within 30 minutes of application, but results can vary from person to person.
special_populations: Children: Brimonidine is generally not recommended for children under 2 years of age due to the risk of serious breathing problems and low blood pressure. Use with close medical supervision in young children. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness and low blood pressure. Use with caution and inform your doctor of any other medications you take. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of brimonidine during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Kidney or liver disease: Let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
